title: How to read a lab report
excerpt: Purity, strength, sterility and endotoxins: what each line on a certificate of analysis means, and what to look for.
content:
Every batch we ship has a lab report. Here's how to read one in two minutes.

Identity

Is it the right molecule? The lab checks its mass and compares it with a known standard.

Purity and strength

Purity is how much of the vial is the peptide. Strength is whether there's as much as the label says.

Sterility and endotoxins

For anything injected, these matter most. Both must pass, every time.

title: What "compounded" means, and what it doesn't
excerpt: Compounded medicines are made for one patient by a licensed pharmacy. They're legal, regulated and not FDA approved. Here's the difference.
content:
A compounding pharmacy makes a medicine for one patient, from a prescription.

Who regulates it

State pharmacy boards license and inspect compounding pharmacies.

What it isn't

Compounded medicines don't go through FDA approval, so testing every batch matters.

Why we publish results

So you don't have to take our word for it.

title: Your first video visit, step by step
excerpt: Twenty minutes, a photo ID and your questions. What to expect when you meet your provider for the first time.
content:
Most first visits take about twenty minutes.

Before

Fill in the health form and have a photo ID nearby.

During

Your provider asks about your health and goals, and answers your questions.

After

If a treatment suits you, the pharmacy starts your order the same day.

title: Injecting at home for the first time
excerpt: Small needles, a quiet minute and a sharps box. Sara from our care team walks you through it.
content:
Most people are surprised how small the needle is.

Get ready

Wash your hands, wipe the top of the vial and the skin with a swab.

Inject

Pinch a little skin on your tummy, put the needle in at an angle and press slowly.

Afterwards

Put the needle straight into the sharps box, and call us with any questions.

title: Sleep, food and movement come first
excerpt: No peptide replaces the basics. Dr. Okonkwo on the three habits she asks every patient about.
content:
Every plan starts with the same three questions.

Sleep

Seven hours, at roughly the same time each night.

Food

Mostly whole foods, enough protein and plenty of water.

Movement

Something every day, even a walk.
